rows.en: <operator(23010,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Holland<ce()>. Once I reach where <color(4)>Eureka<ce()> is, what should I do?
<operator(23030,1)><speed(2)>Ah... My bad. Haven't thought of a thing.
<operator(23010,2)><speed(2)>Thought so.
<operator(23030,1)><speed(2)>Huh?
<operator(23010,2)><speed(2)>Don't beg for things. Do it yourself, or else you won't get anything. Right, <color(4)>Holland<ce()>?
rows.notes: Source line matches the locked Eureka Seven motto (terms_028.json 'Eureka Seven motto', official dub wording) structurally (nedaru na, kachitore, sasureba ataerarenn); used verbatim per the lock, with the source's added 'sou desho, Holland?' appended.

rows.en: <operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>Heh... Those words weren't meant for me.
<operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>Huh?
<operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>They were probably sent to you, through me.
<operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>From <color(4)>Adroc Thurston<ce()> to <color(4)>Renton Thurston<ce()>.
rows.notes: 'Adroc Thurston' (no k) per character_names_021.json/encyclopedia_021_b.json/encyclopedia_022.json lock; Renton's late father.

rows.en: <operator(23010,2)><speed(2)>Yeah!
<operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>Go on... And go pour your heart out to <color(4)>Eureka<ce()>!
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Barrel<ce()>, I want to let those two meet.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>Yeah. Let's go... <color(4)>Faye<ce()>!
<operator(12031,1)><speed(2)>Captain <color(4)>Amuro<ce()>, please look after the two of them.
rows.notes: 'Captain' for taii per terms_028.json lock (Gundam-series pilot rank); tag scope matches source (color wraps only 'Amuro').

rows.en: <operator(5010,1)><speed(2)>Yeah... Two people who care for each other, torn apart. I never want to see something that sad again.
<operator(10020,2)><speed(2)>Man, talk about lovey-dovey. <color(4)>Renton<ce()>'s too embarrassing to even watch.
rows.notes: 'ateraecha' (getting secondhand embarrassment from a couple's PDA) rendered as 'lovey-dovey ... embarrassing to watch'.

rows.en: <operator(10030,1)><speed(2)>Says that, but... You're actually envious, aren't you.
rows.notes: 'urayamashii' rendered 'envious' rather than 'jealous' to avoid the lowercase j.

rows.en: <operator(10020,1)><speed(2)>Wha... N-no, that's not it!
<operator(10010,2)><speed(2)>Let's go. We finally made it back, after all.
<operator(10010,2)><speed(2)>Let's get those two together - this time, we grab our own happiness too!
<operator(25010,2)><speed(2)>Heh heh... Finally made it back. Up for a match, for old times' sake?
<operator(25020,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Isamu<ce()>... Think about those two right now.
<operator(25010,2)><speed(2)>Pretty thoughtful, coming from you.
<operator(17070,1)><speed(2)>...<color(4)>Garrod<ce()>.
<operator(17010,1)><speed(2)>I know, <color(4)>Tiffa<ce()>. No need to sweat the details. We'll make sure they meet!
<operator(17030,2)><speed(2)>Ultimate romance, huh.
<operator(17030,2)><speed(2)>Saving the world and saving your girl, all in one go.
<operator(17020,1)><speed(2)>This isn't the time to be kidding around, is it?
rows.notes: 'chakasu' rendered 'kidding around' rather than 'joking around' to avoid the lowercase j.

rows.en: <operator(23040,2)><speed(2)>That kid's really grown up, hasn't she.
<operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>Yeah... And she used to be only a little tyke.
rows.notes: 'just' avoided mid-sentence (lowercase j); 'only' substituted. 'squirt' avoided (lowercase q); 'tyke' substituted.

rows.en: <operator(23040,2)><speed(2)>Let's send her off, then - our own kid, setting out on her way.
<operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>Tch, graduating on us without asking.
<operator(23200,1)><speed(2)>Must be nice, being <color(4)>Eureka<ce()>. Having someone risk his life for you like that.
<operator(23240,1)><speed(2)>Quit being greedy! You've got one too, don't you - a man named Dominic.
rows.notes: Speaker 23240 = Jurgens (captain of the Izumo per character_names_021.json); addressed as 'Captain' by Dominic in the next row.

rows.en: <operator(23230,1)><speed(2)>C-Captain!
<operator(23200,1)><speed(2)>Heh, that's true.
<operator(23200,1)><speed(2)>I've got Dominic. Way more handsome than <color(4)>Eureka<ce()>'s guy, too!
<operator(21010,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Renton<ce()>... this time it's my turn to help.
<operator(21030,2)><speed(2)>Look at you, saying nice things. You're getting more polished as a man.
<operator(21150,1)><speed(2)>It's great that you two get along, but let's get moving already!
<operator(21020,2)><speed(2)>These kids sure keep leaving the nest, one after another.
<operator(14030,1)><speed(2)>Anyone working hard for a woman is a friend of mine! Gotta help him out.
<operator(19050,1)><speed(2)>Reminds me of when I was reckless like that.
<operator(17040,1)><speed(2)>Building the future... Just as D.O.M.E. said. We can't afford to lose either.
rows.notes: Sentence-initial 'Just' kept (capital J), matching established corpus practice; D.O.M.E. per glossary.

rows.en: <operator(19010,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Renton<ce()>. Let's be sure to get him there.
<operator(19020,2)><speed(2)><color(4)>Go<ce()>... Glad to hear you say that.
<operator(19030,1)><speed(2)>Let's do this.
<operator(14010,1)><speed(2)>Just wait... We'll carve the way open, with our own strength!
<operator(1020,1)><speed(2)>That single-minded devotion of his - we must never let it turn into something sad.
<operator(14010,1)><speed(2)>Yeah... let's go!
<operator(12061,1)><speed(2)>Aww, this is such a swoony drama. You don't see this every day.
<operator(12071,1)><speed(2)>If you asked me what it's for, I'd say - it's for <color(4)>Renton<ce()>.
<operator(12061,1)><speed(2)>We've absolutely got to help him out!
<operator(17070,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Heero<ce()>... Please look after the two of them.
rows.notes: '-san' dropped, consistent with established corpus practice.

rows.en: <operator(6011,1)><speed(2)>I know.
<operator(17070,1)><speed(2)>I can sense it. There's someone waiting for you... Please come back, for their sake too.
<operator(6011,1)><speed(2)>Mission understood.
<operator(19040,1)><speed(2)>Helping with love isn't my style, but I guess I can't say that now...
<operator(19050,1)><speed(2)>From here on, it's their era. We'd better put in some effort for them.
<operator(16040,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Asap<ce()>, please help those two meet again.
<operator(16010,1)><speed(2)>I know. If I were in their place, I'd do the same.
<operator(16040,2)><speed(2)><color(4)>Asap<ce()>...
<operator(12121,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Tenkawa<ce()>. I know what you're thinking.
rows.notes: Speaker 12121 = Genichiro Tsukiomi addressing Akito Tenkawa by surname, per speaker_lookup.py/character_names_021.json.

rows.en: <operator(12011,1)><speed(2)>No need to hide it... I only want to make sure they meet. That's all.

uncertainties.issue: Full Eureka Seven motto quoted; used the locked official-dub wording per terms_028.json verbatim, with the source's trailing 'Right, Holland?' appended to the same row.
'ateraecha' (secondhand embarrassment at a couple's PDA) rendered as 'lovey-dovey ... too embarrassing to watch'; idiomatic, not literal.

Speaker 23240 identified as Jurgens (captain of the U.F. ship Izumo per character_names_021.json); confirmed by Dominic's reply 'C-Captain!' in the next row. No prior scene file uses this speaker id to cross-check.
'koi no tetsudai nante shou ni awanee' (helping with romance isn't my style) rendered loosely as 'Helping with love isn't my style'; idiomatic.
Tsukiomi addresses Akito by surname 'Tenkawa' (source has no honorific); kept as a plain surname address.

checked_decisions: 0/23 Eureka Seven motto ('nedaru na, kachitore, sasureba ataerarenn'): used verbatim per terms_028.json lock, with source's trailing 'sou desho, Holland?' appended to the same row. Confirmed correct per orchestrator ruling.
1/300 speaker 23240: confirmed = Jurgens via speaker_lookup.py; corroborated by Dominic's 'C-Captain!' reply in the next row. Confirmed correct per orchestrator ruling.

1/99 'ateraecha' (secondhand embarrassment at a couple's PDA) rendered idiomatically as 'talk about lovey-dovey ... too embarrassing to watch' - not literal but faithful to the sense and tone. Accepted.
1/579 'koi no tetsudai nante shou ni awanee' rendered loosely as 'Helping with love isn't my style' - idiomatic, meaning preserved. Accepted.
1/659 Tsukiomi addresses Tenkawa by plain surname (source has no honorific) - matches source register. Accepted.

1/460 'that single-minded devotion' (no explicit possessor in source): referent is Hikaru Ichijyo, the immediately preceding speaker (14010) whose line is quoted with passion; gender not inferred from name, drawn from established character. Accepted.
No lowercase j/q found outside locked names anywhere in the scene (checked mechanically); translator's deliberate substitutions (envious, simply, tyke, kidding around) hold up.

All <...> command tags verified identical and in source order for every row; no newlines; ASCII only; no bare %; all 64 rows within the 120 visible-char limit (checked mechanically against tools/scene_source.py output).
